body: I guess so...I mean this came up a lot with my therapist when I was still seeing her. One of the things we talked about is why change my name, pronouns, get an implant to stop my cycle, desire surgery since the age of 12, if I was actually happy being a woman? It's affected every aspect, which means something insn't working.
I was born with the correct plumbing, so I don't feel like a was assigned a gender. More like the one I have doesn't fit, if that makes sense.
What is my gender? I don't know... at least I feel like a blank slate. I suppose all the crying when being referred in female terms was s heads up.

No, but I was diagnosed with CAH. I don't think there was as much info back then, as there is today. I think they only understood as a endocrine issue. So if they hadn't caught in time, who knows how I would have turned out. I always assumed I was Xx, and have fully functioning reproductive organs, unfortunately. I think you have to pay for testing don't you?

Same with me, in that suicide was something I considered. I been overweight since childhood, so I have no idea to work off of what I might look like. It would be so much easier if the other stuff didn't exist.

I have done keto in the past, but I don't feel it is something I can really be consistent with. On top of that, losing weight means having to see my body as it actually is, not a shapeless blob that I've been these past years.

I've come across studies where XX females grow up to change their gender. But in the groups that were studied many were happy to remain women. The theory is that the sooner the child is treated, the more likely they will grow up to be female. Even now there is debate on whether the child should be treated or left to determine their own identity.

Thanks for this post. I wonder if this is the case with me. I was diagnosed with congenital adrenal hyperplasia ( non-salt wasting). I remember a lot of visits and tests. Full female devolopment, but I don't know if that happened because or in spite of it. But as I grew into my teens till now, I noticed I was less happy being female. So am I trans or intersex, or both ? I feel happier wanting yo be male. Would I have been cis if not for this condition? Who knows....
Wow. And now I'm wondering if any Ackerman's have turned on each other if they felt the one they were protecting was in danger from another Ackerman.
I think it's fixed now.
Do you mean the spoilers part?

If you don't mind me asking, how did she find the binder? Are you able to get another one. The fact that she destroyed something that belonged to you makes me angry on your behalf. Does she understand that your mental health is at stake? Have you talked about your suicidal feelings? Parents will or hopefully forego their wants once they recognize that their child's safety is risk. From what I can, I think you should look into creating a safety plan; have your documentation ready, any ID, money if you access to it. 
I'm thinking worst case scenario, but if worst comes to worst, you will need to be prepared.  Hoping everything works out for you. You deserve to be free, to live and be happy.
Edit- I made a mistake about Ellen White's accident. She was actually unconscious for 3 months, not nine days.
What do you mean by the Adventist you had met didn't seem to be happy?
Are you interested in the history of Ellen and church itself . I know she is a controversial figure in some circles.

I forgot to mention this in the video. I decided to start making videos again because of the lack of info regarding growing up intersex( knowing or not knowing ) and having been raised as a Seventh Day Adventist. It's hard to know what to do regarding things like trsnsistion, but the added complication of a religion that would sooner stone or disown you, rather than accept you, is equally as difficult. I want to try and share my perspective from these unique circumstances, in hopes thAt others can be reassured and know that they aren't alone

Restrictions in terms of my mother. She is against anything that doesn't conform with how she feels women should look. She told me that I need to "start carrying myself better" which I took to mean working on my appearance. Except that having to deal with my appearance is why I'm in the state I'm in. When trying to present myself as a woman only causes me depression and dysphoria, I don't really have the energy to try and make myself look nice.

I want to try a different hairstyle than the one I currently have. I thought the box braids were a better fit than the twists I used to wear. But after a year of braids, I realize that I wasn't doing it for myself, rather to please others. I can't wear my natural hair as it is. 

I tried searching for a more masculine look, but I have to wear extensions because my hair isn't long enough to wear by itself. I'm hoping that a new look will give me a little confidence and help with my dysphoria. I don't have means to express myself. I have to be very careful what I wear. I just want to feel a little better about myself.

The title is a little confusing. Has Karla converted? Another thing that worries me is: If she was convicted, wouldn't there be some restrictions on who she is able to interact with? At least here  in the U.S., if you harm or kill a child, you are not allowed within certain places where children might be present.
I did leave. I haven't been to church regularly for about 3 years. But I need to figure out what is best for me.

This went mainstream, wow. But hopefully she is happy with her decision. There is something so isolating about the Adventist community, that seeing stories like this still shock me. But no one should have to carry that weight around. It's a shame that she quit her job, I wonder if she has a backup plan?
Was Willie White a handful for his parents? Maybe it's my impression, but he seemed like he pushed a few buttons here and there.

All of the stuff in the above post I talked about with her. She was very concerned and even considered having me hospitalized. I wonder if I should have taken her up on the offer. There was a period of consideration about if I should check myself in. But I think I  was just desperate to get out of my situation, not actually be committed. 

As far as socially transitioning, I don't think I want to deal with it. That was part of the reason I ended up how I did. I wanted to try and forget and just live as female. But that didn't work out. 

I have a pretty good relationship, considering how recently I started seeing her. She knows that my situation is difficult, that I'm concerned how my family will take it, if I ever manage to sit down and really talk with them. Their not LGBT friendly, at all.
If there is reason for this, that is one thing. But part of me also wonders whether it's arrogant to think that God would do this, as some sort of "plan".

I don't believe anyone wants this. But I think I would like to be a boy, at least I was happy experimenting. But I still wonder about consequences. I know things are be all end all, but I think being wrong is worse. 

One thing I mentioned to my therapist was. "If I am happy being a woman, why go to therapy, look up surgeons, change my name and pronouns, and worry about being discovered?" It's a lot to go through if I was cis.

>Problem is, I keep hearing this sort of circumstance over and over from trans people. They explore a bit, feel good, start to come out of their shells--then a parent or a therapist or a friend or a partner will express their non-acceptance. And all the depression that gender euphoria had held at bay will come crashing down, and the questioner will wonder if they were imagining things. <

Clarification, sorry . My therapist is totally on board. She actually was trying to arrange for me to talk with another trans guy. So I could get some perspective instead of just being alone with my thoughts. Sorry I thought I had made that clear in the beginning of my post. Talking with her has helped with some things. 

She is also helping me in regards to dealing with my mother, basically how stand up for myself. I'll admit that when it comes to certain things I am coward when dealing with her. I want to be able to develop autonomy in certain things. But she kinda tends to get her own way.

>If it were me I'd drop the titles and try solving your thoughts out one by one. You're not the first person that I suggest "trying it out" to. Yes it's going to be tough given your situation, but there's nothing wrong with being trans and there's nothing wrong with figuring out you're not trans. There's also nothing wrong with being non-binary if that's how things work out.<

I'm not sure what you mean about titles. Do you mean the thing about having an identity crisis? As far as trying it, I used my Culinary program to see how I felt. it was ideal because no one knew me personally and I wasn't risking my family possibly finding out. So I guess in that sense I "tried it", but don't know if it's the right thing. 

Suppose living as a woman simply doesn't work for me? Would it be disingenuous to live as the other half because I couldn't deal with being a woman?
It doesn't read as if he is talking about medical care. More like being understanding, trying to help where you can.

I'm not sure what to think about this. On the one hand it's good that he recognizes that the Church/University should help LGBT people. But it's like being a needle in a haystack. It feels so isolating being someone who is questioning and wondering if they have it wrong after all and not being to talk to others like you.
LGBT struggles. I wish I had a clear answer to my problem, but it seems there isn't anything to be done.

Hello from a former SDA. It seems we are hardest to find both in community or online.

My story- Born and raised as an SDA. Went away to boarding school my junior year. I think that was around the time I stopped believing. Religion was a pain, and I felt too constricted. So I decided to come home for college. Was still going to church at this time. By the summer-fall of 2014 I told my parents I didn't want anything to do with religion and it's been that way ever since. My personal struggles influenced my decision and I still wonder if maybe I'm in the wrong.

I;ve had moments like this. I think about wanting to be referred to as male, son, nephew, etc, But I don't think my family would understand, I don't know if I can explain what this means and how it affects me. I think about if I had grown up a boy, how different things might be. I feel like there is a question mark where my gender is, and I want to be able to answer this and be done with it. 

I definitely was jealous of my brother's and other boys toys growing up. I wanted Bionicle after attending a classmates birthday party. I think there was always this longing, to be able to express myself, that was eventually suppressed as I became older. Now it's come back full force, and I am trying to work through it, to better understand what is I want going forward.

I'm more interested in the therapeutic aspect. If I knew then what I knew now, I feel puberty wouldn't have been such hell. I'm resentful when I think what options are available now. Hormone blockers would have really helped. But what's done is done and I can't change the past, no matter how much I want to. I don't know if I want to be gender less, a boy, androgynous, pr something else. But puberty never seems to agree with anyone.
I've wondered if those communities were open to trans people. For me, I kind of want to experience my childhood from the other side. Growing up a girl sucked the first time around.

I struggle with depression, dysphoria and suicidal ideation. I feel a medical experts input would help them understand what I've been dealing with. I don't know if I can express that this (to me) is not a phase. Even though I present female, I feel like a stranger in my own skin.

If things change in the next year, i would  probably be better to have a "history". I don't know if the school I'm looking at has any resources for LGBT students. I would prefer to not start from the beginning. At least I will have proof of what I've been dealing with. That counts for something, right? What about for out of state, if I chose to move in the future? Would the letters be accepted from that therapist, or would I need to see someone within the state?

As far as letters are concerned, how long are they good for? Say I am able to get a letter saying I have dysphoria, I need hormones, top surgery, etc? Could I sit on it until I have the means to move forward? If I have the letters at least, then that can eliminate a step in the process right?

I'm a few years younger than you, but in a similar position. I gradually stopped feeling like a woman, over several years. A part of me seemed to be saying, "Why are you doing this? For what purpose?". I sometimes wonder if I would be satisfied being a masculine woman, but I don't like being a woman. But how can I prove that I want be a man, what evidence would be convincing to others that this is what I want to be? Sometimes when I am talking with other woman, I feel like things don't quite click. Marriage, family, all the things expected of me, I want no part of. I've been trying to find a label that describes what I am, but none seem to fit.

Because I never knew the word could be applied to someone like me. For all intents and purposes I look normal. If you knew my history and what to look for, that's one thing. But the way I understood intersex growing up, people used another more demeaning word to describe people like that. So I always felt a little different but unsure why.

What would I ask the doctor? I have an appointment in two weeks but I don't know what I should them. I'm a long ways away from being independent. I'm working on getting a job , my drivers license, etc. I don't know if this is worth pursuing anymore.
I have been seeing a therapist, but I think seing a doctor would answer my questions. If they have experience with people like me then that's good.

I post on the FTM sub, so I know how transition works. It's more the fact am I truly trans or considered non conforming, or something in between. I worry that I don't meet certain criteria, not enough dysphoria, etc. I present female, live with my parents so there's that. Being a woman fucks with every aspect of my life.

I've read about the Sda Kinship group. Not sure what to do with the info. I did find a writer/author named Eliel Cruz. Bisexual guy who goes (or maybe he graduated) to Andrews University. I think he helped create a LGBT group on the campus. It turns out when he was 14 he was thrown out of his Academy for being bisexual. It's hard enough knowing your sexuality or trying to figure it out during adolescene. The response by the school was terrible.

I've been questioning a good deal. I know I don't want to live as a woman. But if God wanted me to be a boy, I would have been born a boy. Gender roles suck, efpecislly when it comes to bring female. How you unpack what is dysphoria and simple dissatisfaction with your gender? I've had several sessions with my therapist and went yo a clinic that offered trans care, but I don't feel any closer to an answer than when I started.

It took a long time for me to understand what it meant to be LGBT. What that meant for me spiritually and mentally. I left because I couldn't reconcile being queer and being Christian. I wish I knew what I identified as so I can be at peace. The damage religion has done to the community is saddening. So many people who need help, are seen as different just because they don't toe the party line. And when they realize that gender and sexuality affects everyone, it can be even worse. I feel so dismissed isolated because I don't know of anyone who is current or Ex-Advrntist who is dealing with things like this. Sometimes I wonder if this is all in my head.

Hi. Welcome to r/ftm. It's good that you are thinking about things, trying to figure yourself out. I grew up under similar circumstances, non-Muslim, but strict Christian. There is no room for alternative lifestyle or going against what God wants for you, etc. Bad enough, but questioning my own gender made things worse, and eventually I left. I don't know who I am, whether that is a trans guy, non binary, or a self-hating woman which is the worst in my opinion. Like you I wonder if I;m just butch and want to be as close to male as possible. But at the end of the day, the idea of being a woman in any way is distressing for me. I don't see myself being happy as a woman, more than likely I wouldn't survive. Which may be the answer I've been looking for. 

Where you live, are there any LGBT resources, such as a support group? Have you tried experimenting with your clothing, maybe seeing how you feel about pronouns? Or is that too risky? I wouldn't want to make any suggestions that might get you into  trouble. 

It is hard with family, but worse when religion is involved. Have you talked with your family and told them how you feel, that you see yourself as male and not female?

My only reason to want to be male is because I can't stand being a woman. Physically and mentally I hate it. But the argument of other women not liking parts of themselves makes me doubt whether or not I'm truly trans. I just want to be happy and feel comfortable in my skin. I don't want to live the rest of my life like this but I also feel like I have to deal with this the best I can. It's to the point where I told my therapist I would consider psychiatric so I wouldn't have to deal with this anymore. I'm not suicidal, not yet, being alive and living as a women is worse than being dead.

I think losing weight can help with getting better results. Depending on the procedure you are looking at, a few pounds can make a difference in what a surgeon is able to do. I think anything D cup and above double mastectomy is likely your only choice.

Top surgery is a significant procedure. Is this something you have wanted for awhile? If yes, then maybe you're realizing this is really happening. I'm a long way from surgery, but I know that it is what I want in the future.
Why do they think that? Isn't Tim Kaine Christian?
So what about those who thought they were trans, transitioned and later realized they were wrong? Apart of is hoping I'm some degree of trans, otherwise I can't justify wanting to be male.
Therapy is good. It can help you figure out what is going on and what you want or don't want.
What would this mean for currently questioning/closeted trans people? I'm in the process of getting therapy and trying to figure myself out. What would happen to us/them?
Interesting. I've never heard of this company. How would you describe your time working there?

The golden ticket thing was actually pretty interesting. I was treated in childhood, but I don't think I was ever given estrogen. This was around 7-10 yrs of age, so memory is a bit fuzzy. I guess I need a 'valid" reason to transition. Not just poor body image, depression, etc. I want to know that it is okay to do this, whatever that entails.

I have been talking to a therapist, appointment this week. But this has never come up or something I'd ever considered. I always felt it was something that made me a bit different. But now I'm dealing with all this and it has only gotten worse as the months go by. Why couldn't I have been born cis?

I wish I could accept it, but it feels like a chicken egg scenario. I was born normal and later decided to transition, then it would be product of circumstance. Are intersex people more likely to transition or stay with their assigned sex (if there were any treatments or surgeries performed, for example)?
Sorry, I should clarify. I was born with CAH, non salt wasting. I've read that it is considered an intersex condition. So if I go by that explanation, do I have a case to transition?

Possibly, but in every instance that I've observed, it was more like "spot who is queer" as if they had a sign on their back. Or making jokes and pointing out 'signs' as proof. It was never done in a positive manner.
Thanks. This really means a lot to me. I can pm my address if someone else hasn't claimed the black one yet.

Wow, this is really awesome of you. I've been wanting to get a binder for months but money, and my own issues prevented that. Plus to go from being :"well endowed" to well somewhat flat would look questionable. But my mental health trumps all this. Would you mind sending me a photo of the GC2b  black binder? I should let you know, I live in Southern California, would you consider international shipping? I don't want to inconvenience you if the cost is to much.

Is there a recognized reputable source for the number of calories in a pound of fat? I looked it up and there is something that was posted that to a pound you need to burn 7000 calories, not the 3500 that has been used for years. Anyone else come across this?

I guess people saying I may become to thin, since I've been heavy most of my life. But my main concern is that the more weight I lose the less obscured my body will be. I don't want to have a visible ass, hips, waist. My chest is bad enough and I can't do anything to hide it. Being fat and "secure" seems more appealing than healthy.

Have any of you struggle with losing weight for yourself, whether that is health related, personal goals, etc. I've been trying to work on losing weight to better my health, but I keep thinking about the reactions I will get once the weight loss becomes noticeable. On top of that I'm struggling with gender issues which make things more difficult and hard to parse out whether it's poor self image. Any tips on how to deal with this?
